nodes.label: Patient-split duplication bug (fixed)
nodes.rationale: Provided code built training rows once per held-out patient and concatenated five copies, duplicating every beat ~5x and leaking test-patient beats; explains handout's 25,789 beats per class. Would have hidden part of the generalisation drop.

nodes.label: PermFIT (permutation feature importance with K-fold cross-fitting)
nodes.norm_label: permfit (permutation feature importance with k-fold cross-fitting)
nodes.rationale: Model-agnostic, global explanation; cross-fitting (K=5 stratified folds) ensures each beat is scored by a model that did not train on it. Importance = increase in squared error of predicted class probabilities; variance and p-values not estimated as instructed.

nodes.label: PermFIT limitations (global, correlated slices, fixed windows, fold leakage)
nodes.norm_label: permfit limitations (global, correlated slices, fixed windows, fold leakage)
nodes.rationale: In-PermFIT CV accuracy 96-99% vs 84-87% on unseen patients because upsampled copies cross folds; patient-grouped folds recommended. Explains what a model uses, not whether it generalises.

nodes.label: PermFIT slice importance results (Table 4, Figures 4-5)
nodes.rationale: Slice 6 (R-peak) dominates; QRS share 98.2%/94.9% (SVM) and 83.7%/85.3% (RF). RF spreads importance to QRS edges (slices 4 and 8); RF profile nearly identical across protocols (Pearson r=0.999).

nodes.label: Perturbation sensitivity check (zero, mean, swap/permute)
nodes.rationale: Shuffle and mean agree because both keep slice level; zero and swap change level and make ST segment important (QRS share drops to 83% SVM / 63% RF). Slice 6 remains top under all 16 combinations; report more than one perturbation.

nodes.label: Platt scaling (CalibratedClassifierCV, ensemble=False)
nodes.rationale: SVM gives no probabilities; Platt scaling calibrates scores while keeping the SVM decision boundary, needed for PermFIT's squared-error importance.

nodes.label: Hypothesis: QRS slices 5-7 most important
nodes.rationale: Cardiology places most diagnostic information in the QRS complex; supported by results (84-98% of importance in slices 5-7, R-peak slice 6 top in all 16 model/protocol/perturbation combinations).

nodes.label: Random forest (300 trees)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as contrast to the SVM: trees ask threshold questions about single time points while the RBF SVM compares whole-beat shape. Better on beat hold-out (96.8%) but worse on unseen patients (83.6%), suggesting it learns patient-specific detail.

nodes.label: RBF Support Vector Machine (SVC)
nodes.rationale: Default C=1, gamma='scale', one-vs-one; patient hold-out version adds StandardScaler and max_iter=10000. Default C kept so explained models equal evaluated ones, though grid search favours C=100.

nodes.label: Perturbation: shuffle within slice (main method)
nodes.rationale: Follows the case study; destroys slice shape but keeps mean and variance.

nodes.label: Kernel SHAP (linear LIME + Shapley values)
nodes.rationale: Uses LIME objective with Omega(g)=0, Shapley kernel pi_x'(z')=(M-1)/((M choose |z'|)|z'|(M-|z'|)) and squared loss, recovering Shapley values. Slide title spelled 'Kernel SHARP'.

nodes.label: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations)
nodes.rationale: Locally faithful, accessible to non-experts, retains model flexibility; model-agnostic so switching costs are small. Gives qualitative understanding of input-response relation.

nodes.label: Multicollinearity in feature importance
nodes.rationale: Feature importance may be underestimated when features are collinear; SHAP addresses this by averaging over all feature subsets.

nodes.label: SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations)
nodes.rationale: Each explanation treated as a surrogate model; game theory guarantees a unique solution satisfying local accuracy, missingness and consistency, so it improves over LIME and handles multicollinearity. Drawbacks: exponential subset evaluation, high cost even with KernelSHAP, local approximators may still not reveal model behaviour, ignores time-series dependencies.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Resampling (sklearn resample, up/down-sampling)
nodes.rationale: Target count per class = mean of abnormal class totals; all 8 training classes resampled to 3990 (beat holdout) or 25789 (patient holdout).

nodes.label: ECG Beat 11-Segment Slicing (PR 1-4, QRS 5-7, ST 8-11)
nodes.rationale: Beats divided into 11 segments (data points replaced by slice average) so PFI reveals which morphological region (PR interval, QRS complex, ST segment) the classifier relies on.

nodes.label: Model-Agnostic Approaches (model/explanation/representation flexibility)
nodes.rationale: Preferred because they offer model, explanation and representation flexibility: same technique applies to any fitted estimator.

nodes.label: PermFIT (Permutation-based Feature Importance Test, cross-fitted)
nodes.rationale: Algorithm 1 of Mi et al. 2021: split data into K folds, train model on out-of-fold data, compute per-subject importance M_ij^(P,CV) as squared-error increase after permuting feature j on held-out fold, then aggregate M_j and estimate its variance for significance testing.

nodes.label: Permutation Feature Importance (PFI)
nodes.rationale: Model inspection technique for any fitted (esp. non-linear/black-box) estimator: importance = drop in score when a single feature is randomly shuffled, breaking feature-target relationship. i_j = s - (1/K) sum_k s_{k,j}. Global method explaining whole dataset, not individual samples. Disadvantages: no in-depth understanding, ignores feature interactions, cannot give exact/local explanations needed for legal/ethical reasons; adds randomness.

nodes.label: Explainable Models
nodes.rationale: Knowing which input factors affect the output and by how much; needed because black-box models (NNs) do not reveal why they reach an output or when they succeed/fail.

nodes.label: Interpretability vs Accuracy Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Complex models (SVM, deep learning) offer better accuracy but are inherently less interpretable than linear regression / decision trees; KNN and random forests sit in the middle.

nodes.label: Interpretable / Transparent Models
nodes.rationale: Model readily understandable, direct explanation, cause and effect can be determined; e.g. decision trees, linear and logistic regression.

nodes.label: Random Forest Beat Hold-out Slice Importance
nodes.norm_label: random forest beat hold-out slice importance
nodes.rationale: All methods peak at slice 6 (~0.37-0.51); permute and zero spread importance to slices 4, 7, 8 (out-of-distribution artefacts), while shuffle and mean stay concentrated at slice 6.

nodes.label: ECG Slice 6 Importance Peak (shaded slices 5-7)
nodes.rationale: Shaded region 5-7 likely marks the QRS complex; slice 6 is most important for both models regardless of perturbation, showing the main finding is robust.

nodes.label: SVM Beat Hold-out Slice Importance
nodes.rationale: All four perturbations peak sharply at ECG slice 6 (~0.85-1.14 mean importance M_j), secondary at slice 7; other slices near zero. Permute gives slightly elevated baseline across non-QRS slices.
